docs.text: as a transplant from new orleans to chicago, i think we should make one of these fuckass bridges over lake michigan

Tonight we’re staying downtown so we can be on the Chicago Riverwalk early in the morning. Periodically in the spring and fall, there are bridge lifts for the purpose of folks moving their vessels in/out of Lake Michigan to/from boat storage. We’ve always wanted to see it, so we’re going.

Obviously you can do this without building a bridge over Lake Michigan. I'm not an engineer, but I don't think it would be impractical. Actually probably more practical than the land use implications of the alternative? Anyway, not the longest bridge in the world by a long shot.

Penultimate bridge lift of season (and it’s not a lock the last, next Wednesday, won’t be cancelled.) Four sailboats making their way in the rain up the Chicago River to Lake Michigan. Spring went by fast.
Someone once wondered on socials why no one has built a bridge across Lake Michigan connecting IL/WI with MI and I just laughed

Wednesday bridge lift, 9 sailboats making the journey up the Chicago River to Lake Michigan

Chicago Loop theatre folks: The Fall bridge lift season starts in earnest tomorrow morning, as sailboats start coming in off Lake Michigan heading to winter storage. Allow extra travel time the next few Saturday (and I believe Wednesday) mornings if coming into the Loop.
Last scheduled Saturday bridge lift of the season. Five sailboats make their way down the Chicago River to Lake Michigan
